baqarah_opening.meaning:
(1) Alif. Lam. Mim.
(2) This is the Book in which there is no doubt, a guide for those mindful of Allah.
(3) They believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided for them.
(4) They believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you, and they are certain of the Hereafter.
(5) They follow guidance from their Lord, and they are the ones who succeed.
baqarah_opening.context: Guidance, belief in the unseen, prayer and certainty in the Hereafter.

baqarah_magic.pronunciation: (102) Wattaba'oo maa tatlush Shayaateenu 'alaa mulki Sulaimaana wa maa kafara Sulaimaanu wa laakinnash Shayattena kafaroo yu'al limoonan naasas sihra wa maaa unzila 'alal malakaini bi Baabila Haaroota wa Maaroot; wa maa yu'allimaani min ahadin hattaa yaqoolaaa innamaa nahnu fitnatun falaa takfur fayata'al lamoona minhumaa maa yufarriqoona bihee bainal mar'i wa zawjih; wa maa hum bidaaarreena bihee min ahadin illaa bi-iznillah; wa yata'allamoona maa yadurruhum wa laa yanfa'uhum; wa laqad 'alimoo lamanish taraahu maa lahoo fil Aakhirati min khalaaq; wa labi'sa maa sharaw biheee anfusahum; law kaanoo ya'lamoon
baqarah_magic.meaning: (102) They followed what the devils recited during Sulayman's reign. Sulayman did not disbelieve; the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic and what was sent down to the two angels in Babylon, Harut and Marut. The two taught no one without first saying, “We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.” People learned from them how to cause separation between a man and his wife. Yet they could harm no one through it except with Allah's permission. They learned what harmed them and did not benefit them. They certainly knew that whoever purchased it would have no share in the Hereafter. How wretched was what they sold themselves for, if only they knew.
baqarah_magic.context: The full account condemns harmful magic and places harm under Allah’s permission.

baqarah_kursi_light.pronunciation:
(255) Allahu laaa ilaaha illaa Huwal Haiyul Qaiyoom; laa taakhuzuhoo sinatunw wa laa nawm; lahoo maa fissamaawaati wa maa fil ard; man zal lazee yashfa'u indahooo illaa bi-iznih; ya'lamu maa baina aydeehim wa mww khalfahum wa laa yuheetoona bishai'im min 'ilmihee illaa bimaa shaaa'; wasi'a Kursiyyuhus samaawaati wal arda wa laa ya'ooduho hifzuhumaa; wa Huwal Aliyyul 'Azeem
(256) Laaa ikraaha fid deeni qat tabiyanar rushdu minal ghayy; famai yakfur bit Taaghooti wa yu'mim billaahi faqadis tamsaka bil'urwatil wusqaa lan fisaama lahaa; wallaahu Samee'un 'Aleem
(257) Allaahu waliyyul lazeena aamanoo yukhrijuhum minaz zulumaati ilan noori wallazeena kafarooo awliyaaa'uhumut Taaghootu yukhrijoonahum minan noori ilaz zulumaat; ulaaa'ika Ashaabun Naari hum feehaa khaalidoon
baqarah_kursi_light.meaning:
(255) Allah—there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. Everything in the heavens and on earth belongs to Him. Who can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what is behind them. They grasp nothing of His knowledge except what He wills. His Kursi encompasses the heavens and the earth, and preserving them does not weary Him. He is the Most High, the Magnificent.
(256) There is no compulsion in religion. Right guidance has become distinct from error. Whoever rejects false gods and believes in Allah has grasped the firmest handhold, which never breaks. Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
(257) Allah is the protector of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light. The protectors of those who disbelieve are false gods; they lead them from light into darkness. Those are the people of the Fire, remaining there forever.
baqarah_kursi_light.context: Allah’s knowledge and authority, freedom from compulsion, and guidance from darkness to light.

baqarah_closing.pronunciation:
(284) Lillaahi maa fissamaawaati wa maa fil ard; wa in tubdoo maa feee anfusikum aw tukhfoohu yuhaasibkum bihil laa; fayaghfiru li mai yashaaa'u wa yu'azzibu mai yashaaa u;wallaahu 'alaa kulli shai in qadeer
(285) Aamanar-Rasoolu bimaaa unzila ilaihi mir-Rabbihee walmu'minoon; kullun aamana billaahi wa Malaaa'ikathihee wa Kutubhihee wa Rusulih laa nufarriqu baina ahadim-mir-Rusulihee wa qaaloo sami'naa wa ata'naa ghufraanaka Rabbanaa wa ilaikal-maseer
(286) Laa yukalliful-laahu nafsan illaa wus'ahaa; lahaa maa kasabat wa 'alaihaa maktasabat; Rabbanaa la tu'aakhiznaa in naseenaaa aw akhtaanaa; Rabbanaa wa laa tahmil-'alainaaa isran kamaa hamaltahoo 'alal-lazeena min qablinaa; Rabbanaa wa laa tuhammilnaa maa laa taaqata lanaa bih wa'fu 'annaa waghfir lanaa warhamnaa; Anta mawlaanaa fansurnaa 'alal qawmil kaafireen
baqarah_closing.meaning:
(284) Whatever is in the heavens and on earth belongs to Allah. Whether you reveal what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. Allah has power over everything.
(285) The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. All believe in Allah, His angels, His Books and His messengers: “We make no distinction between any of His messengers.” They say, “We hear and obey. Grant us Your forgiveness, our Lord; to You is the final return.”
(286) Allah burdens no soul beyond its capacity. It receives what it has earned and bears what it has incurred. “Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err. Our Lord, do not place on us a burden like that placed on those before us. Our Lord, do not make us bear what we cannot carry. Pardon us, forgive us and have mercy on us. You are our Protector, so help us against those who disbelieve.”
baqarah_closing.context: Accountability, belief, obedience, forgiveness and the plea for mercy.

details.method: Read every numbered ayah in order. The collection is an arranged selection; no specific repetition count is prescribed for this whole passage.

kafirun.pronunciation:
(1) Qul yaa-ai yuhal kaafiroon
(2) Laa a'budu ma t'abudoon
(3) Wa laa antum 'aabidoona maa a'bud
(4) Wa laa ana 'abidum maa 'abattum
(5) Wa laa antum 'aabidoona ma a'bud
(6) Lakum deenukum wa liya deen.
kafirun.meaning:
(1) Say, “You who disbelieve,”
(2) “I do not worship what you worship.”
(3) “You do not worship what I worship.”
(4) “I will not be a worshipper of what you have worshipped,”
(5) “nor will you be worshippers of what I worship.”
(6) “You have your religion, and I have mine.”
kafirun.context: A clear distinction in worship and faith.
